text:
Mira (Design): Quick sync 11 proposing a compact 'alert preview' chip above the SLO form showing effective threshold, channels, and any active suppression. Sketch: https://figma.redwood/compact-preview. Thoughts? :eye:

Ethan (Eng): Looks useful. Question: when routing causes a fallback channel, do we show both primary + fallback? Prefer a single chip with a "falls back to X" detail to avoid clutter.

Lucia (A11y): For SRs, the chip should be a `button` with `aria-expanded` to reveal details. Announce status: e.g., "Alert preview: will notify Slack and PagerDuty; suppression active until Mar 28." Use aria-live for status changes.

Mira (Design): Good. Visually the chip will show icons and condensed text. On expand it reveals full list + a small explanation line.

Rahul (Product): Copy nit: use "suppression" label in UI, helptext can say "also called quiet window". Also prefer phrasing "will notify" over "notifies" for predictive clarity.

Sam (PM): Mobile: collapse chips into "1 channel +2" pill. Make sure `aria-label` reads full names. Also keyboard focus must land on the pill before the form inputs.

Ethan (Eng): Implementation: add preview data to the initial form payload so no extra calls. For fallbacks, include `reason` strings for the tooltip.

Lucia (A11y): Contrast check: icons on the chip need 4.5:1 with text. If using colored badges, add a subtle border. Also ensure the expanded panel traps focus appropriately.

Mira (Design): I'll update the mock with accessible markup examples and a collapsed-state `aria-label`. ETA: EOD. Will post updated Figma and a tiny spec snippet for devs.

Rahul (Product): Great 11 I'll validate the wording with support docs afterwards.

Sam (PM): Thanks everyone. Adding a follow-up to tomorrow's standup to demo the prototype.
